To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

XRCC1Arg39Gln polymorphism is associated with a decreased risk of breast cancer (p = 0,006), XRCC3Thr24Met polymorphism is associated to an increased risk of this disease (p < 0,001) and RAD51G135 polymorphism is associated as risk factor for familial breast cancer (p=0,012).
XRCC1Arg39Gln and XRCCC3Thr241Met are important biomarkers to breast cancer susceptibility and RAD51G135 is a risk modifier for breast cancer susceptibility in familial cases.
XRCC1Arg/Gln, XRCC3Thr/Met and RAD51G135 polymorphisms are genetic indicators for sporadic and familial breast cancer susceptibility, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the importance of DNA repair genes as potential genetic biomarkers of susceptibility to breast cancer, and it could be useful to improve early diagnosis and prevention of this disease.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the role of DNA repair genes in breast cancer susceptibility is not yet fully understood.
DNA repair polymorphims are not only important biomarkers of breast cancer susceptibility, but also risk modifiers of familial breast cancer cases.
XRCC3ThrMet polymorphism seems to have the strongest association with sporadic breast cancer, and that RAD51G135 polymorphism is a risk modifier in familial cases of breast cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
XRCC1399 and XRCC3241 polymorphisms are associated with sporadic breast cancer, RAD51135C polymorphism with familial cases and XPDLys751 polymorphism with both types of breast cancer.
XRCC1Arg/Gln, XRCC3ThrMet and RAD51Gly/Cys are genetic indicators of sporadic and/or familial breast cancer susceptibility.
XRCC3ThrMet polymorphism could be considered a risk factor for breast cancer susceptibility, and RAD51G135CC genotype would be a risk modifier for familial breast cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DNA repair polymorphims might be important biomarkers to breast cancer susceptibility.
XRCC1399Arg/Gln and XRCC3241Thr/ Met polymorphisms are important genetic markers for sporadic breast cancer, whereas the RAD51135G/C polymorphism is associated with familial cases.
the genetic profile of breast cancer susceptibility may be more complex than it is currently believed.
